question.problem: Find the volume of the solid region enclosed by the $xy$-plane, the surface $z=y\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ and the planes $x=0,$ $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ $y=0,$ $y=1.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[z]_{z=0}^{z=y\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x-0\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x(\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-0)\,dx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\operatorname{sin}⁡x]_{x=0}^{x=\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
